name: ZS and The Birthday Paradox
description: ZS the Coder has recently found an interesting concept called the Birthday Paradox. It states that given a random set of 23 people, there is around 50% chance that some two of them share the same birthday. ZS the Coder finds this very interesting, and decides to test this with the inhabitants of Udayland. In Udayland, there are 2 n days in a year. ZS the Coder wants to interview k people from Udayland, each of them has birthday in one of 2 n days (each day with equal probability). He is interested in the probability of at least two of them have the birthday at the same day. ZS the Coder knows that the answer can be written as an irreducible fraction . He wants to find the values of A and B (he does not like to deal with floating point numbers). Can you help him?
input_specification: The first and only line of the input contains two integers n and k (1 ≤ n ≤ 10 18 , 2 ≤ k ≤ 10 18 ) , meaning that there are 2 n days in a year and that ZS the Coder wants to interview exactly k people.
output_specification: If the probability of at least two k people having the same birthday in 2 n days long year equals ( A ≥ 0 , B ≥ 1 , ), print the A and B in a single line. Since these numbers may be too large, print them modulo 10 6 + 3 . Note that A and B must be coprime before their remainders modulo 10 6 + 3 are taken.
approach_summary: Precompute linear sieve to store minimum prime factor (spf[x]) up to N in O(N). Factorize any number x ≤ N in O(log x) steps.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 711E — ZS and The Birthday Paradox [242. Sieve, Prime Factorization and Divisors]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Every composite integer $X$ has at least one prime factor $\le \sqrt{X}$. Precomputing the Smallest Prime Factor (SPF) for all numbers up to $M$ via a linear sieve allows any $X \le M$ to be completely prime-factorized in $O(\log X)$ steps.
